title: Scenario Kernel Projection Conformance
description: Recorded evidence that a language's strict-TypeScript structural projection provider, driven by its projection profile, reproduces that language's admitted structural shape. This is a computed observation document, not hand-authored authority.

profilePath.description: Repo-relative path to the scenario-kernel-language-projection-profile.v1 instance this observation used.

disposition.description: Explicit evidence closure. NOT_OBSERVABLE means the required target toolchain could not be exercised; it is distinct from a projection defect.

toolchainValidation.description: The real compiler/type-checker's verdict on the generated files alone (dotnet build / tsc --noEmit / mypy --strict). Proves the generated code is VALID; does not by itself prove it MATCHES the admitted shape — that is structuralComparison's job. Neither is sufficient alone, matching the finding that motivated this schema: generated code can compile cleanly while still being semantically wrong relative to admitted authority.

handWrittenOnly.description: Types present in the hand-written source with no generated counterpart — e.g. a profile whose objects[] list doesn't yet cover every hand-written type.

generatedOnly.description: Types the projector produced with no hand-written counterpart to compare against.

conforming.description: True iff toolchainValidation.conforming is true AND structuralComparison shows zero mismatches, zero handWrittenOnly, and zero generatedOnly. The single verdict downstream consumers (evaluates-projection-conformance.js) read — everything else on this document is supporting evidence for a human, not something a consumer should re-derive.
